correctness.rationale: The Hessenberg condition reduces to existence of a hyperplane containing \(P+SP\), equivalently \(P\cap SP\ne0\). In Plücker coordinates this is the Grassmannian quadric together with the determinant quadric. Their pencil has exactly three singular members, each with a two-dimensional coordinate kernel, giving exactly six base-locus singular points. On every coordinate chart the transverse quadratic form is nondegenerate, so all six are ordinary double points. The exceptional fibers over the invariant two-planes are exactly \(\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1\), hence the birational map is small. Abe--Fujita--Zeng identify the anticanonical line bundle with the Hessenberg weight; here it is \(2\varpi_1+\varpi_2\), which descends to the partial flag target and is ample there. Normal Gorensteinness plus smallness gives crepancy. A fresh symbolic reconstruction independently verified the determinant identity and the factorization needed for the node test; the bundled checker also verifies all six Hessians and the localization value \(192\).
correctness.risk: The conclusion is specific to the stated four-dimensional regular semisimple Hessenberg function.

final_claim: For regular semisimple \(S\) and \(X=\operatorname{Hess}(S,(3,3,4,4))\), forgetting the three-plane is the anticanonical contraction onto a \(\mathbb P^1\)-bundle over a \((2,2)\) complete intersection in \(\mathbb P^5\) with exactly six nodes; the contraction is small and crepant, with six exceptional \(\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1\) surfaces, and \((-K_X)^4=192\).
limitations: Base field \(\mathbb C\), regular semisimple \(S\), and exactly \(h=(3,3,4,4)\).
No general classification of weak-Fano Hessenberg anticanonical models is claimed.
